topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the lecture's core learning objectives.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology: genetics, environment, and epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the fundamental causes of cancer by examining the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, microenvironmental support, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological variations.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the oncogenic mechanisms of infectious pathogens, using Burkitt lymphoma and Epstein-Barr virus as an in-depth case study.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe specific physical and chemical mutagens and the metabolic processes that convert them into DNA-damaging adducts and reactive compounds.

topics.label: Tumour promotion, physiological susceptibility, and multistage carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how non-mutagenic factors—including tumour promoters, chronic inflammation, and developmental timing—cooperate with initiating mutations to drive cancer progression.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogenicity and evaluating risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro techniques for identifying carcinogens and the practical risk-benefit considerations surrounding human exposure.

topics.label: Lecture summary and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing and final summary of the lecture.
